閥.meaning: Five lumberjacks <part>fell</part> trees only for each other. They build a private <part>gate</part> from the logs and give a key to nobody else. Inside, they wear matching checked shirts and laugh at their own jokes. Outsiders call them a <kanji>clique</kanji>.
閥.on: To join, you need a secret <sound>bu</sound>tton sewn onto your shirt.

閲.meaning: At the castle <part>gate</part>, a fussy <part>imp</part> with a magnifying glass checks every visitor: their boots, their hats, the spelling in their letters. Mistakes get a red mark. Nobody gets in until he has done a full <kanji>review</kanji>.
閲.on: The best guests get a tiny <sound>etch</sound>ing of the castle as a prize.
閲.kun: Those who pass get tea from a <sound>ke</sound>ttle carried by a <sound>mee</sound>rkat.

岳.meaning: A <part>hill</part> wanted to be taller, so it climbed on top of a <part>mountain</part>, like a kid on its dad's shoulders. Together they poke right through the clouds and end in one needle-sharp <kanji>point</kanji>, where eagles queue to perch on the peak.
岳.on: A <sound>ga</sound>ggle of geese lands on the tip and squabbles over who's highest.
岳.kun: A climber at the top unpacks a <sound>ta</sound>co and a little <sound>ke</sound>ttle.

桃.meaning: A fortune teller reads the future in fruit, not tea leaves. She plucks one from her <part>tree</part>, studies its fuzz and finds a <part>portent</part>: 'You'll be sticky by noon.' She bites in and juice runs down her chin. It came true: a <kanji>peach</kanji>.
桃.on: A drop of juice lands on her bare big <sound>toe</sound>.
桃.kun: She wipes it up with a <sound>mo</sound>p, while a <sound>mo</sound>th sips the last drop.

克.meaning: For years the <part>old</part> tug-of-war champion has beaten every <part>big brother</part> in the village. This year one skinny big brother trains all winter, drags him over the mud line, and helps him up with a bow. Fear, mud and a legend: he managed to <kanji>overcome</kanji> them all.
克.on: A <sound>coc</sound>katoo on the fence screeches the new champion's name.
克.kun: He keeps perfectly <sound>ca</sound>lm for one second, then dances in the mud: to win.

奔.meaning: A <part>large</part> man sleeps in and runs for the train with a whole <part>bush</part> still tangled in his beard from his camping trip. Leaves fly, pigeons scatter, porters leap aside. His dash sets the whole station into a <kanji>bustle</kanji>.
奔.on: Taxis outside join in, <sound>hon</sound>king their horns.
奔.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs a <sound>shee</sound>p in the next carriage as he sprints past.

犠.meaning: A <part>cow</part> wins the blue ribbon at the fair, then sees that the judges cheated a little goat out of it. Out of pure <part>justice</part>, she hands the ribbon over and walks home with nothing. Giving up what you love for what's right: <kanji>sacrifice</kanji>.
犠.on: The goat thanks her by fixing the broken <sound>gear</sound> on her milking machine.
犠.kun: At home she has an <sound>ee</sound>l pie, a <sound>ke</sound>ttle of tea, a rug over her <sound>knee</sound>s and one boiled <sound>e</sound>gg.

牲.meaning: In a dry summer, a <part>cow</part> has grown just one flower in her whole field, the only bit of <part>life</part> left. She carries it gently in her mouth to the village shrine and leaves it there for the rain gods. Her one flower is her <kanji>sacrifice</kanji>.
牲.on: That night the rain comes, and the priest locks the flower in a <sound>sa</sound>fe.

伯.meaning: At the fire station, a <part>white</part> helmet hangs on a <part>coat hook</part> by the pole. When the bell rings, whoever grabs it first gives the orders that day. The crew slide down in a heap, and the spotted station dog trots past them, helmet in its teeth. Today it barks the orders: the <kanji>chief</kanji>.
伯.on: Its reward that evening is a whole <sound>huc</sound>kleberry pie, eaten off the fire truck's bumper.
